subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw own for side-effecting external secret providers under service supervisors?
rationale: Automation can prove the current fail-fast path, but only maintainers can choose the security/product tradeoff between fail-closed startup, bounded retry, degraded startup, circuit breaking, and external resolver/plugin delegation.

options.title: Generic bounded startup policy
options.body: Add a core-owned bounded retry/backoff or degraded-startup policy for required SecretRef activation failures, with tests and docs that avoid 1Password-specific behavior.

options.title: Resolver/plugin delegation plus docs
options.body: Keep startup fail-fast in core and document supervisor restart limits plus external resolver batching/caching, such as Varlock, as the supported mitigation.

options.title: Configurable retry surface
options.body: Add an explicit SecretRef retry policy or provider option, accepting the added config and upgrade-safety burden.

recommendation.title: Generic bounded startup policy
recommendation.body: Add a core-owned bounded retry/backoff or degraded-startup policy for required SecretRef activation failures, with tests and docs that avoid 1Password-specific behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history connection to the SecretRef provider and runtime snapshot behavior that this decision would change.
